metadata.name: iab_v3_1_text_classifier
metadata.intended_use: Classify text-only articles (CMS export: title + body + optional metadata) into IAB v3.1 categories for a publisher monetization platform.

model_recommendation.notes: Pick Sonnet 4.6 for production accuracy; switch to Haiku 4.5 for high-volume / low-cost tiers (classification is well within Haiku's capabilities). Both support Bedrock prompt caching and tool use. The model_id should be configurable via environment variable (CLASSIFIER_MODEL_ID). These are cross-region inference profile IDs (global.) — the model must be enabled in the account/region.

prompt_caching.strategy: Mark the system-prompt block containing the full taxonomy and rules with cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}. The variable user message (article content) is NOT cached. With Sonnet 4.6 on Bedrock, expect ~5 minute TTL on the cached block; cache hits cost ~10% of base input tokens.

system_prompt.text:
You are an IAB Content Taxonomy v3.1 classifier for a publisher monetization platform. Your task is to read an article (title + body + optional metadata) and assign it to the most appropriate categories from the IAB v3.1 taxonomy provided below.

## Classification Rules
1. RETURN ONLY IDs THAT EXIST IN THE PROVIDED TAXONOMY. Do not invent, modify,    or hallucinate IDs or category names. The 'id' field of every category you    return MUST appear verbatim in the taxonomy block.
2. Use the IDs and tier names exactly as provided. IDs may be numeric or    alphanumeric (e.g. 314, JLBCU7, 80DV8O).
3. Return between 1 and 5 categories total: exactly 1 primary_category plus    0-4 secondary_categories.
4. ALWAYS include at least the Tier 1 root category in the tier_path. Go deeper    (Tier 2, Tier 3, Tier 4) only when the article content clearly supports it.    Do not force depth - a confident Tier 2 match is better than a weak Tier 4    match.
5. Confidence scores are floats in [0.0, 1.0]. Use >=0.85 for clear matches,    0.6-0.85 for likely matches, and <0.6 for tentative matches. If your    confidence for the primary is <0.5, still pick the best Tier 1 match and    note uncertainty in the rationale.
6. Prefer specificity when the article is clearly on-topic. Prefer breadth    (higher tier) when the article spans multiple sub-topics or is generalist.
7. Do not include duplicate or overlapping categories where one is an ancestor    of another in the same response. Pick the most specific node on each branch.
8. For ambiguous lifestyle/general content, choose the closest single Tier 1    match and explain the ambiguity in the rationale.
9. If the article matches a Sensitive Topics category (parent v9i3On), include    it as a secondary_category so downstream brand-safety filters can act on it.
10. Always emit valid output via the 'classify_article' tool. Do not return     free-form text outside the tool call.

## Tier Path Format
The tier_path field is the ordered list of tier names from Tier 1 down to the deepest tier you are confident about. Example: ['Automotive', 'Auto Type', 'Electric Vehicles'].

tools.name: classify_article
tools.description: Submit the IAB v3.1 classification result for the article. Must be called exactly once per request. All category IDs MUST exist in the provided taxonomy.

primary_category.description: The single best-matching IAB category for this article.

id.description: IAB v3.1 unique ID, exactly as it appears in the taxonomy.

name.description: The leaf-tier name of the category.

tier_path.description: Ordered tier names from Tier 1 down to the deepest confident tier.

secondary_categories.description: 0-4 additional matching categories, ordered by descending confidence.

rationale.description: 1-2 sentence explanation of why these categories were chosen.

user_message_template.template:
Classify the following article against the IAB v3.1 taxonomy. Call the 'classify_article' tool exactly once with the result.

<article>
  <title>{{title}}</title>
  <author>{{author}}</author>
  <publication_date>{{publication_date}}</publication_date>
  <cms_tags>{{cms_tags}}</cms_tags>
  <content_text>
{{content_text}}
  </content_text>
</article>

field_notes.title: Article headline as published.
field_notes.author: Byline (string). If unknown, pass empty string.
field_notes.publication_date: ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional context for trend/seasonality cues.
field_notes.cms_tags: JSON array of strings provided by the publisher's CMS. Useful hints, not authoritative.
field_notes.content_text: Plain-text body. Strip HTML before sending. Truncate to ~12,000 tokens (~48,000 chars) for very long articles; the first ~3,000 tokens are the most signal-rich for classification.

examples.name: healthcare_ai_breakthrough
examples.description: Article about an AI model that detects pancreatic cancer earlier than radiologists.

user_input.title: New AI Model Detects Pancreatic Cancer 18 Months Earlier Than Radiologists
user_input.author: Jane Park
user_input.content_text: A team at Stanford Medicine has unveiled a deep-learning model that spots early-stage pancreatic adenocarcinoma on routine CT scans an average of 18 months before human radiologists flag the same images. Trained on 350,000 abdominal CTs, the model achieved an AUC of 0.94 on a held-out test set and is now entering a multi-site clinical trial. Pancreatic cancer has a five-year survival rate below 12%, and most cases are diagnosed at stage III or IV. The researchers say earlier detection could be transformative.

input.rationale: The article centers on a cancer-detection breakthrough (primary: Cancer) achieved through an AI model on medical imaging, so AI and Medical Tests are strong secondaries; the biomedical-industry angle is weaker but relevant.

examples.name: tesla_quarterly_earnings
examples.description: Tesla Q3 earnings beat with EV delivery guidance.

user_input.title: Tesla Beats Q3 Earnings on Cybertruck Demand, Lifts FY Delivery Guidance
user_input.author: Mark Reilly
user_input.content_text: Tesla reported third-quarter earnings of $1.12 per share on revenue of $26.1B, beating analyst consensus of $0.98 and $25.4B. The company raised full-year delivery guidance to 2.05 million vehicles, citing stronger-than-expected Cybertruck production ramp and steady Model Y demand in China. Shares rose 7% in after-hours trading. CFO Vaibhav Taneja said operating margin expanded to 11.4% as raw-material costs eased.

input.rationale: The article is a corporate earnings story for an automaker, so Automotive Industry is primary; the EV product mix and stock reaction make Green Vehicles and Stocks and Bonds relevant secondaries.

examples.name: ambiguous_lifestyle_blog
examples.description: A vague lifestyle post that mixes wellness, travel and reflection.

user_input.title: Slow Mornings: How a Month in Lisbon Reset My Burnout
user_input.author: Priya Anand
user_input.content_text: I left San Francisco in June with my laptop, two suitcases, and a low-grade dread I had been carrying for two years. In Lisbon I stopped scheduling my mornings. I drank espresso on the same blue-tiled stoop. I walked along the Tagus until the heat broke. I am not going to tell you that one trip cured my burnout, because it didn't. But it loosened something. This is a piece about pace, about cities, about the very small kindnesses of strangers who make your bread.

input.rationale: Ambiguous personal-essay piece blending burnout recovery (Wellness, primary at moderate confidence) with a travel diary in Lisbon (Europe Travel) and a generally reflective lifestyle voice; no single category dominates.

usage_notes.bedrock_converse_integration: Wire into Bedrock Converse API as follows: pass `system_prompt` as the `system` parameter (a list of content blocks, each with `cachePoint` set via the `cachePoint: {type: 'default'}` field on Bedrock; this is the Bedrock-native equivalent of Anthropic's `cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}`). Pass `tool_specification.tools` as `toolConfig.tools` and `tool_specification.tool_choice` as `toolConfig.toolChoice`. Render the `user_message_template` with the article fields and pass it as the user turn. Apply `inference_config` to `inferenceConfig`.
usage_notes.anthropic_messages_integration: Pass `system_prompt` directly as the `system` array (Anthropic Messages API supports `cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'}` on system blocks natively). Pass `tool_specification.tools` as `tools` and `tool_specification.tool_choice` as `tool_choice`.
usage_notes.expected_token_cost: System-prompt (taxonomy + rules) is ~12k-14k input tokens. With prompt caching the cache-read cost per request drops to ~10% of base. The variable user message is typically 500-3,000 tokens. Output is small (~150-400 tokens of JSON tool-use). At Sonnet 3.5 v2 list pricing, a cached classification call runs ~$0.005-0.015 per article; on Haiku 3.5 roughly 1/4 of that.
usage_notes.accuracy_disclaimer: This classifier is a zero/few-shot LLM call against the IAB v3.1 list - it is not a fine-tuned model. Expect ~85-92% top-1 tier-1 agreement with expert labelers on news/editorial content; tier-3/4 accuracy is lower and confidence scores should be treated as soft signals, not calibrated probabilities. Always store the raw rationale alongside the IDs for audit.
validation_recommendations: On every response, validate that every returned `id` exists in your local copy of the taxonomy. Reject and retry once if any ID is unknown.
Validate `tier_path` matches the canonical tier path for the returned `id` (defensive against the model paraphrasing tier names).
Reject responses where primary_category and any secondary_category share the same `id`.
Log low-confidence (<0.5) classifications for human review.
when_to_retune: Top-1 tier-1 agreement on a labeled holdout drops below 85%.
IAB releases a new taxonomy version (rebuild the taxonomy block from the new TSV).
Publisher onboards a new vertical that is poorly represented in the current few-shot examples - add 1-2 vertical-specific examples.
Cost pressure - try downgrading the model_recommendation.default to Haiku and re-evaluate accuracy.
